title: How can letters go on counting past z?
description: The letters a to z count only twenty six objects, so longer groups of letters are added after z. The video uses doubled letters, then tripled letters, matching objects with letters in order as in the example in the book, and checks that no group repeats.
teaching_notes: One idea: a counting sequence of letters never runs out if longer groups of letters can always be made. Each new length gives twenty six more places. Many schemes work, so accept any that gives every object its own group and never stops.

source: Figure it Out (the mechanism of counting, question 2)
video_script.why: The child extends the letter method past z by making longer groups of letters, keeping the fixed order that a number system needs.
video_script.substitution: List the groups of letters in order: one letter, then two letters, then three letters, and count the places each length adds.
video_script.anchor: a row of objects with the letters a to z under the first twenty six and an empty box under the twenty seventh
video_script.payoff_line: Longer groups of letters never run out

final_answer.value: One way: a to z, then aa, bb, ..., zz, then aaa, bbb, ..., zzz and so on; many other ways work
final_answer.spoken: one way is eigh to zed, then doubled letters, then tripled letters, and so on, and many other ways work

hold_back: One way: a to z, then aa, bb, ..., zz, then aaa, bbb, ..., zzz and so on; many other ways work
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: a to z count objects 1 to 26
26 + 26 = 52, so aa, bb, ..., zz count objects 27 to 52
52 + 26 = 78, so aaa, bbb, ..., zzz count objects 53 to 78
each longer length adds 26 more places, and a longer length can always be made, so the sequence never ends
check: object 27 is aa, object 52 is zz, object 53 is aaa; no group is used twice and none is skipped
